answer: Histories are stored in beacon, checked in kernel, and nectar makes public each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 6 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm cannot present clean aliases because the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. A farm of 1557 identities would post 4253 proofs and burn roughly 21 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
